titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§154–157: The Tatars Destroyed, Jesügen and Jesüi, and the Wang Qan's Raid
part: §§154–157 — The Tatars Destroyed, Jesügen and Jesüi, and the Wang Qan's Raid
about: Four sections. §154: after the Tatars have been broken, Chinggis Qahan takes counsel alone with his kin in a tent and resolves to kill every Tatar measured against a cart's linchpin and enslave the rest; Belgütei, asked by Jeke-Chelen what was said, lets it out, the Tatars fortify, and the army suffers badly in the assault, so Chinggis bars Belgütei from the council. §155: Yesügen Qatun, a Tatar chief's daughter, is taken by Chinggis, tells him her elder sister Yesui would suit a qan better than she, and the sister is found and seated above her. §156: at a feast Yesui sighs, Chinggis has the tribes stand apart by clan, and a young stranger is picked out and beheaded. §157: a short report of the Wang Qan's raid on the Merkid in the Dog year, which ends with Chinggis given nothing. The councils of §154 and the two women's speeches in §155 lean heavily on the Ming glosses, and a number of readings are marked as first readings in the notes.

sentences.t: Tatar-i muqudγažu daγ̇ulin baražu ulus irgen an-u ker kikün keġen
sentences.l: Tatar-ACC wiping-out, plundering, being-finished, realm people, their, how doing-shall, saying,
sentences.i: "Having wiped out and plundered the Tatars and finished them, what shall we do with their realm and people?" — so saying,
sentences.n: The Ming 麽道 (keġen, 'saying') closes a thought that opens the next unit: this is what Chinggis asked. The first three verbs are a converb chain (muqudγažu, daγ̇ulin, baražu: 'wiping out, plundering, finishing'), and I have cut the chain here and left kikün keġen ('shall we do, saying') as its end. muqudγa- is my inference from the Ming 絕 'cut off'; I cannot analyse it further. an-u is 'their', the back-vowel partner of in-ü. kikün is ki- 'to do' with the participle -kün; the Ming writes it 做咱 'let us do'. I take the whole as an indirect question about the people left after the war, which is how the next unit reads.

morph.gloss: to wipe out, destroy (stem inferred from the Ming 絕 'cut off') [敎絕着]
to be finished, used up, ruined [了着]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm [百姓]
their (third-person genitive, back-vowel companion of in-ü, set after its noun) [他的]
participle: 'that which will be done' (with ker, 'how shall we do')

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan jeke eje uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan γaγča ger-tür orožu ejetüldübe.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, great counsel, with-kin-own, alone, house-in entering, took-counsel-together.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan went alone into a tent with his own kin and took great counsel.
sentences.n: A plain sentence, verb last. γaγča orožu 'alone entering' is one chain; ger-tür is ger 'house, tent' with the dative-locative -tür ('in', Ming 裏). ejetüldübe is eje 'counsel' made into a verb and given the reciprocal (Ming 共商量了 'consulted together'), with the past -be. The oddity is uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan (Ming 一族 自的行): I read uruk 'kin', then -jar, which elsewhere in these parts is an instrumental ('with'), then the reflexive -(i)jan; the bracketed (i) is Shiratori's. 'With his own kin' fits the Ming, but the middle piece is a guess.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
kin, kinsfolk (Ming 一族) [一族 自的行]
to take counsel together (eje 'counsel' + a verbal -tül- reciprocal; Ming 共商量) [共商量了]

sentences.t: Ejetüldürün: "Erte üdür-eče Tatar irgen ebüges ečigeš-i baraγsan büleġe.
sentences.l: Counselling-together-when: "Formerly from days, Tatar people, ancestors, fathers-ACC ruining was.
sentences.i: In that counsel he said: "In former days the Tatar people ruined our ancestors and fathers.
sentences.n: A quotation opens at Erte (the opening quotation mark is printed on it). ejetüldürün is the same verb as before with the converb -rün, Ming 商量說道 'saying in counsel'; I take it as the verb of speaking. erte üdür-eče is 'from early days' (ablative -eče). ebüges ečigeš-i are ebüge and ečige with the plural -s, with the accusative -i written 行 by the Ming; 'ruined' is baraγsan büleġe, a participle with 'was', i.e. a past perfect. 'Our' is not in the Mongol, but ancestors and fathers of whom? The next sentence makes it plain that they are the speakers' own.

morph.gloss: to take counsel together [商量說道]
to be finished, ruined (here transitive: 'to ruin') [廢盡的]

sentences.t: Ebüges ečiges-ün öšül öšüžü kisal kisažu čiγ̇un-dur uližu kidužu alažu öġüje;
sentences.l: Ancestors, fathers' vengeance avenging, grudge requiting, linchpin-at comparing, destroying, killing, let-us-give;
sentences.i: Let us avenge the wrong done to our ancestors and fathers and settle the grudge: let us measure them against the linchpin, destroy them and kill them.
sentences.n: Two paired objects (öšül/kisal) with their verbs (öšüžü, kisažu), then a converb chain of four: uližu, kidužu, alažu, öġüje. The linchpin (čiγ̇un, Ming 車轄) is the cart's axle-pin, and uli- is 'to compare' (Ming 比): the plain sense is to match the people against the pin and kill all who reach it; the text itself does not say so, and the explanation is the usual one for the formula, not something found in this passage. I have therefore kept 'measure them against the linchpin' and left the rest implied. The last verb is öġü- 'to give' with -je, the hortative (Ming 與咱, 'let us give'); here it stands as a helper after the converbs, and 'let us' covers the series. Unsure.

morph.gloss: grudge, wrong, a score to settle (Ming 仇) [仇]
to requite, to settle a score [報着]
linchpin of a cart (Ming 車轄) [車轄 行]
to compare, to measure (Ming 比 'compare') [比着]
to cut off, destroy utterly (Ming 盡絕) [盡絕着]

sentences.t: ülidtele kiduja; hülegsed-i boγ̇ollduja žüg žüg qubijalduja"
sentences.l: Until-left-over destroying-let-us; remnants-ACC slave-making-let-us, direction direction dividing-let-us"
sentences.i: Let us wipe them out down to the last, and let us make slaves of those who remain and share them out in every direction."
sentences.n: The quotation ends at qubijalduja" (closing mark). ülidtele is read as ülid- 'to be left over' with -tele 'until'; the Ming has only 盡絕 'cut off to the end', so the analysis is mine. hülegsed-i 'those who remained' (past participle, plural -d, accusative -i; Ming 剩的(每)行) is the object of boγ̇ollduja, boγ̇ol 'slave' with a verbal ending and -ja 'let us' (Ming 奴婢做使咱). žüg žüg is 'side by side, every quarter'. Three -ja 'let us' verbs in a row are the whole proposal.

morph.gloss: to cut off, destroy utterly [殺︀着]

sentences.t: keġen eje baraldužu, ger- tēče γaruγ̇asu
sentences.l: Saying, counsel settled-having, house from going-out-when,
sentences.i: Having so settled the counsel, as they went out of the tent,
sentences.n: keġen again closes the quotation. baraldužu is bara- 'to be finished' with the same -ldu- as before, so 'having finished, concluded' (Ming 定了着). The word ger- is printed with a hyphen and its ablative tēče (Ming 行) stands on the next line; I join them as 'from the house'. Note that -tēče is the same ablative as -eče above, written with a long vowel. γaruγ̇asu is γar- 'to go out' with -γ̇asu, the conditional 'when' (Ming 呵). The unit stops short of the main verb on purpose, so the sentence continues in the next one.

morph.gloss: house, tent (printed with a hyphen; the ending -eče follows on the next word) [房子]
ablative: from (long-vowel form tēče; Ming 行 'from') [行]

sentences.t: Tatar-un Jeke-Čelen Belgütei-eče ambar eje ejetüldübe" keġen asaγčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Tatar's Jeke-Čelen, Belgütei-from, "what-sort counsel took-counsel-together" saying, had-asked.
sentences.i: Jeke-Chelen of the Tatars asked Belgütei, "What counsel have you taken together?"
sentences.n: The one Mongol sentence whose subject is a Tatar. Jeke-Čelen is a man of the Tatars (Tatar-un, genitive) and the ablative -eče on Belgütei means 'from Belgütei', so 'asked of'. ambar eje is Ming 怎生商量 'what counsel'; ejetüldübe is the earlier verb, and the quotation marks open and close on the Ming's own line. asaγčuγ̇u is asa- 'to ask' with the past -čuγ̇u (Ming 問了有來, 'had asked'). Why a Tatar should be at hand to ask is not said; I take him to be a Tatar of the household or a go-between, which is a guess.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Chelen, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Belgütei, a man's name (half-brother of Chinggis) [人名 處]
what sort of, how (Ming 怎生) [怎生]
to take counsel together [共商量了]
past tense: 'had asked' (Ming 問了有來)

sentences.t: Belgütei ügülerün: "Tan-i bügüde-ji čiγ̇un-dur uližu kiduja keġeldübe" keġežüġü.
sentences.l: Belgütei speaking-when: "You-ACC all-ACC linchpin-at comparing, destroying-let-us, we-said" said.
sentences.i: Belgütei, speaking, said: "We have said that, measuring against the linchpin, we shall kill you, every one."
sentences.n: Belgütei answers by repeating the plan. Tan-i is the second-person plural 'you' with the accusative (Ming 您行) and bügüde-ji 'all' (accusative); the grammar is of a verb, 'kiduja', and its object 'you all'. keġeldübe is keġe- 'to say' with the reciprocal-past, i.e. 'we (together) said'. keġežüġü ends the sentence ('he said'), as in Ming 說有來. So Belgütei is passing the secret in a few words. Whether he meant it as a warning or was careless is not stated.

morph.gloss: linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to destroy utterly (Ming 盡殺) [盡殺︀]

sentences.t: Belgütei-jin ene üge-dür Jeke-Čelen Tatar-tur-(i)-jan tuṅqaγ talbižu qorγaγlažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Belgütei's this word-in, Jeke-Čelen, own-Tatars-to, notice sending-out, had-fortified.
sentences.i: Because of these words of Belgütei, Jeke-Chelen sent word to his own Tatars, and they fortified themselves.
sentences.n: Belgütei-jin takes the genitive -jin after a vowel, and ene üge-dür is 'in this word', so 'by these words'. tuṅqaγ talbižu is 'putting out a notice' (Ming 傳說 'to pass word'; talbi- 'to put, to let go'); Tatar-tur-(i)-jan is 'to his own Tatars', dative-locative -tur plus the reflexive. The main verb is qorγaγlažuγ̇u, from qorγaγla- 'to make a stockade' (Ming 寨子把 'to hold a fort'), past -žuγ̇u. Who 'they' are is the Tatars, though the Mongol has no plural marker and the subject could be only Jeke-Chelen himself.

morph.gloss: Tatar, the Tatars [種(名) 自的行]
notice, proclamation, word sent (Ming 傳說) [傳說]
to put, to set, to let go [放着]
to fortify, to set up a stockade (Ming 寨子把) [寨子把了來]

sentences.t: Qorγalaγsad Tatar-tur bidan-u čeriġüd eġerekün bolun maši samšižuγ̇u.
sentences.l: The-fortifiers, Tatars-to, our soldiers attacking-about-to, very ruined.
sentences.i: When our army was about to attack the Tatars who had fortified, it was badly ruined.
sentences.n: Qorγalaγsad is a plural participle, 'those who had fortified', and the Ming 寨子把了的(每) says the same. Tatar-tur 'to the Tatars' is a dative of direction (Ming 行). bidan-u čeriġüd is 'our soldiers' (čeri 'soldier' plus the plural -ġüd, Ming 軍每). eġerekün bolun is 'about to attack' (-kün participle, bolun a converb, Ming 做呵). The verb is samšižuγ̇u, 'wasted, ruined' (Ming 廢耗了); I put 'badly ruined' for maši samšižuγ̇u and take it to mean heavy losses. The grammar of the first words (the fortifiers as a kind of topic) is loose, and I have smoothed it.

morph.gloss: plural past participle: 'those who had fortified'
we, our (inclusive, genitive stem bidan-) [咱的]
converb: -ing (the Ming 呵 makes it 'if, when')
to ruin, to waste, to be spent (Ming 廢耗) [廢耗了]

sentences.t: Qorγalaγ- sad Tatar-i žobožü oroγ̇ulžu ülüdgen čiγ̇un-dur uližu kiduqui-dur
sentences.l: Fortifiers, Tatars-ACC, struggling, making-enter, utterly linchpin-at comparing, destroying-when,
sentences.i: When, after a hard fight and forcing their way in, they were killing the fortified Tatars to the last, by the linchpin,
sentences.n: A printed line-break splits Qorγalaγ- from -sad; the join gives the same word as before. žobožü oroγ̇ulžu is 'toiling, causing to enter', Ming 生受着 敎入着 'with effort, making (them) go in'; the sense of the second verb is probably 'forcing them in'. ülüdgen is read as 'to the last' from the Ming 盡絕 'cut off'; I cannot analyse the word. kiduqui-dur is kidu- 'to destroy' with the participle -qui and -dur, 'at the destroying' (Ming 時, 'when'). A break in the long converb chain: the chain restarts in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to fortify (printed with a hyphen; the plural -sad follows on the next line) [寨子把了的]
to toil, to suffer (Ming 生受) [生受着]
remaining to the last, utterly (Ming 盡絕; form unclear) [盡絕]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]

sentences.t: Tatar ügüleldürün:" Küġün tutum qančun-dur(i)-jan kituγai qančulažu dere abun üküje" keġeldüžü
sentences.l: Tatars speaking-together-when: "Man each, sleeve-in-own, knife in-the-sleeve-putting, back taking, let-us-die" saying-together,
sentences.i: the Tatars said among themselves: "Let each man hide a knife in his own sleeve, and let us die taking (an enemy) with us," and,
sentences.n: The one doubtful reading in this unit is dere abun üküje. dere is 'on, upon' and the Ming gives 藉背 'to lean on the back'. abun is ab- 'to take' with the converb -n, and üküje is ükü- 'to die' with -je 'let us' (Ming 死咱). I read 'taking (him) with us (as a cushion/prop)' as an idiom of dying while taking an enemy along; this is the usual translation of the idea, but not something I can show from the Ming. qančun-dur(i)-jan is 'in one's own sleeve' (Ming 袖 裏自的行). ügüleldürün and keġeldüžü are reciprocal forms ('said among themselves'); keġeldüžü is a converb and the main verb is in the next unit.

morph.gloss: sleeve (Ming 袖) [袖 裏自的行]
to put in the sleeve, to tuck away (Ming 袖着) [袖着]
upon, on top; here Ming 藉背 'lean on the back' (reading uncertain) [藉背]

sentences.t: basa maši-kü samšižuγ̇u. Tedüi Tatar-i čiγ̇un-dur uližu kidun baražu
sentences.l: Again very-indeed ruined. So-much Tatars-ACC linchpin-at comparing, destroying, finishing,
sentences.i: And again they suffered very heavy losses. After all that, having measured the Tatars against the linchpin and destroyed them,
sentences.n: samšižuγ̇u is the verb of keġeldüžü's sentence: 'saying so, again they were greatly ruined' (maši-kü, 'very, indeed'; -kü is the emphatic). tedüi is 'so much, so many'; here it stands before Tatar-i in the sense 'those (Tatars)' (Ming 那些). The converbs kidun baražu 'destroying, finishing' hang from the next unit's main clause. I break here because the whole chain from line 84 to the next decree would otherwise have no stopping place.

morph.gloss: to ruin, to waste [廢耗有來]
so much, so many, thus [那些]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to be finished, to finish [殺︀了着]

sentences.t: tende Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun;
sentences.l: There, Chinggis Qaγan decree being-when:
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan issued this decree:
sentences.n: tende 'there' is also 'then'. bolurun is bol- 'to be, to become' with the converb -urun (Ming 說道, 'saying'), the standard formula 'when a decree came into being'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Bida uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan jeke eje baralduγsan-i Belgütei-jin žaγ̇aqu-jin tula bidan-u čeriġüd maši samšijaba.
sentences.l: "We, with-kin-own great counsel finished-ACC, Belgütei's telling because-of, our soldiers very ruined.
sentences.i: "Because Belgütei told what we had settled in our great counsel among our own kin, our army has been badly ruined.
sentences.n: A passage whose logic is clear but whose grammar is not. baralduγsan-i is a past participle 'what was concluded' with an accusative (Ming 了了的 行); žaγ̇aqu-jin tula is 'because of the telling', participle -qu with genitive -jin and the postposition tula (Ming 上頭). The Ming gives samšijaba as 廢耗了 'ruined', and it parallels the earlier samšižuγ̇u. I take 'bidan-u čeriġüd samšijaba' as the result. Whether the whole was meant as a rebuke to Belgütei or as a ground for the exclusion that follows is the reader's reading; the rule is stated in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to be finished, settled [了了的 行]
Belgütei, a man's name [人名 的]
to tell, to report, to declare (Ming 吿) [吿的]
because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭) [上頭]
to ruin, to waste, to be spent [廢耗了]

sentences.t: Eġün-ü qoina jeke eje-dür Belgütei bu orotuγai.
sentences.l: This-of after, great counsel-in, Belgütei not enter-let.
sentences.i: After this Belgütei is not to enter the great council.
sentences.n: eġün-ü qoina is 'after this' (genitive of eġün 'this', Ming 這的後). bu is the prohibitive, with the optative -tuγai on orotuγai 'let (him) enter' (Ming 者). So 'Belgütei: do not let him enter'. The structure is that of a decree: subject, then verb in the jussive.

morph.gloss: do not (prohibitive particle; Ming 休) [休]

sentences.t: Eje baratala γadana bükün-i žasa- tuγai;
sentences.l: Counsel finishing-while, outside being-ACC, ordering-let;
sentences.i: While the counsel is going on, let those who are outside be kept in order;
sentences.n: baratala is bara- 'to be finished' with -tala 'until'; the Ming 了間 gives 'in the time of finishing'. bükün-i is 'those who are', the participle of bü- 'to be' (the -kün ending as in kikün) with the accusative. žasa- (Ming 整治) means 'to put in order, to regulate, to punish'. I put 'kept in order' and ask the reader to keep in mind that the next unit goes on to punishment of offenders.

morph.gloss: to put in order, to regulate, to punish (Ming 整治) [整治]

sentences.t: žasaγ̇ad kereġür-i qulaγai qudal üileten-i žarγulatuγai.
sentences.l: Ordering-having, brawlers, thief, liars, those-doing-business-ACC, let-judge.
sentences.i: and when they have been set in order, let brawlers, thieves, liars and troublemakers be judged.
sentences.n: Five accusatives in a row, one verb. Only kereġür-i and üileten-i take the case ending; qulaγai and qudal are bare nouns (Ming 盜, 謊). üileten-i is üile 'work, business' with -ten 'having' (Ming 勾當有的每 行), i.e. 'those who have business on hand' and, by an overtone of the Ming, 'wrongdoers'. žarγulatuγai is žarγu- 'to judge' with a verbal -la- and -tuγai (Ming 敎斷者, 'let (them) be judged').

morph.gloss: to put in order, to regulate [整治了]
quarrel, brawl (Ming 鬭毆) [鬭毆的行]
work, business (Ming 勾當) [勾當有的每 行]
to judge, to decide a case [敎斷者︀]
optative/jussive: 'let (them) be -' (Ming 敎斷者 'have them judged')

sentences.t: Eje baraγ̇asu ötög ūγsan-u qoina Belgütei, Daγ̇aritai qojar tende orotuγai." keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Counsel finished-when, drinking, those-drank-of after, Belgütei, Daγ̇aritai, two, there enter-let" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: When the counsel is over, after the drinking, let Belgütei and Da'aritai, the two of them, come in." So the decree was made.
sentences.n: baraγ̇asu is bara- with -γ̇asu 'when' (Ming 了呵). ötög ūγsan-u qoina is 'the drink, after having drunk it': ötög (Ming 進酒) with the past participle ūγsan (Ming 飮了的) in the genitive and qoina 'after'. qojar is the numeral for pairs of persons. Daγ̇aritai is a man's name (Ming 人名), of whom nothing else is known here. The decree closes with keġen žarliγ bolba, 'saying, a decree was made'. This ends §154.

morph.gloss: drinking, a drink offered (Ming 進酒) [進酒]
Daγaritai, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.t: Tende Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü ökin Jesügen Qatun-i Čiṅgis Qaγan tende abba.
sentences.l: There, Tatar's Jeke-Čeren's daughter, Jesügen Qatun-ACC, Chinggis Qaγan there took.
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan took Yesügen Qatun, the daughter of the Tatar Jeke-Cheren, as his own.
sentences.n: The § opens with Tende 'there, then'. Jeke-Čeren-ü is a Tatar name (printed Čeren here, Čelen in §154); I take it to be the Jeke-Čelen who was asked in §154, since the Ming has 人名 for both, but the text does not prove it. ökin is 'daughter' (Ming 女), the genitive chain is Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü ökin 'the Tatar Jeke-Cheren's daughter'. abba is ab- 'to take' with -ba (Ming 要了). Jesügen Qatun-i is a woman's name (Ming 女名) with the accusative on Qatun. tende before abba is another 'there', which I pass over.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Cheren, a man's name (Ming 人名; printed Čeren here, Čelen above) [人名 的]
Yesügen, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Taγ̇alaγdarun Jesügen Qatun ügülerün:"
sentences.l: Favoured-when, Jesügen Qatun speaking-when:
sentences.i: Being favoured by him, Yesügen Qatun said:
sentences.n: taγ̇alaγdarun is taγ̇ala- 'to favour' with the passive -γda- and the converb -run; the Ming 被寵的上頭 says 'on account of being favoured'. I put 'being favoured' and leave it unsaid whether the favour came from the Qahan, though the sense points to him. ügülerün is the ordinary 'when speaking'.

morph.gloss: to favour, to hold dear (Ming 被寵) [被寵的上頭]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.t: Qaγan sojurγaγ̇asu nama-ji küġün-e bodo-da bolγažu asaramu;
sentences.l: "Qaγan, if-bestowing, me-ACC person-to, thing-to making, raising-is;
sentences.i: "If the Qahan shows me grace, he raises me up and makes me something among people.
sentences.n: The hardest line of the speech. sojurγaγ̇asu is sojur- 'to bestow' (Ming 恩賜) with -γ̇asu 'if, when'; the printed form is split in the next part of §156. nama-ji is 'me' (accusative, Ming 我行). küġün-e bodo-da bolγažu is 'to a person, to a thing, making'; the Ming 人行 物行 gives nothing more. I read it as 'making me a person, a somebody' and treat bodo as a first reading: it may be a word 'thing' or something else. asaramu is asara- 'to raise, to foster' (Ming 擡擧) with the present -mu. I have kept the sense, not the details.

morph.gloss: to bestow, to show favour (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜呵]
thing, real, actual (Ming 物; reading uncertain) [物行]
to raise up, to foster (Ming 擡擧) [擡擧有]

sentences.t: nadāča egeči Jesüi neretei nadāča deġere qān küġün-e žokiqui ažiγ̇ai že.
sentences.l: Than-me, elder-sister Jesüi named, than-me higher, qan person-to, fitting was, indeed.
sentences.i: My elder sister, who is named Yesui, would suit a qan better than I, for she is of higher rank.
sentences.n: nadāča is 'than me' (the ablative -dāča with a long vowel; Ming 比我), and it comes twice. neretei is nere 'name' with -tei 'having', so 'named' (Ming 名字有的). deġere is 'above, higher' (Ming 高); I take it to mean 'higher in worth', not 'taller'. qān küġün-e žokiqui ažiγ̇ai is 'for a qan-person, fitting, was' (Ming 皇帝人行合宜的有來也者): a modest speech, 'she was the fitting one'. že is a sentence-final particle. ažiγ̇ai is a past 'was' whose form I cannot confirm.

morph.gloss: ablative: than, from (Ming 比我 'than me')
qan, sovereign (the Ming 皇帝) [皇帝]
emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.t: Sai küregen küregelen büligi.
sentences.l: Just-now son-in-law, son-in-law-making, was.
sentences.i: She had only just taken a husband.
sentences.n: sai is 'just now' (Ming 恰纔). küregen is 'son-in-law, bridegroom' and küregelen is a verb from it with the converb -n (Ming 做女壻). Literally 'just now, being a son-in-law, was': her sister had lately married. The Ming gives no more, so 'taken a husband' is my reading.

morph.gloss: just now, only just (Ming 恰纔) [恰纔]
to take as son-in-law, to be a son-in-law (Ming 做女壻) [做女壻]

sentences.t: Edöġe maqa ene bodulγan-dur qaγ̇aγši jorčibi" keġebi.
sentences.l: Now who-knows, this turmoil-in, where gone-has" said.
sentences.i: Now, who knows where she has gone in this turmoil?" she said.
sentences.n: maqa 'unknown' (Ming 不知) is an adverb 'who knows'. bodulγan 'turmoil, upheaval' (Ming 亂離) with -dur is 'in the upheaval' (the war with the Tatars). qaγ̇aγši is 'where to', jorčibi is jorči- 'to go' with the first-person past -bi (Ming 去了), though I take it as 'has gone' and not as a statement of her own going. keġebi ends the quotation, 'I said', but in the English 'she said' is better.

morph.gloss: unknown, who knows (Ming 不知) [不知]
turmoil, upheaval (Ming 亂離) [亂離 裏]

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: This word-in, Chinggis Qaγan speaking-when:
sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Ordinary frame: ene üge-dür 'in this word', and ügülerün 'when speaking'. Nothing needs flagging here.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Egeči čin-u čima-dāča sain bögsen böġesü eriġülüje.
sentences.l: "Elder-sister, your, than-you good, being if, let-us-have-sought.
sentences.i: "If your elder sister was better than you are, let us have her sought.
sentences.n: čin-u is 'your' and čima-dāča 'than you'. bögsen böġesü is the past participle 'having been' with a conditional, 'if she was'. eriġülüje is eri- 'to seek' with the causative -ġül- and the hortative -je: 'let us have (her) sought' (Ming 敎尋咱). The thought is that Chinggis wants to see whether the sister is better, which is his way of taking up her modest remark.

sentences.t: Egeči-jen ireġesü žailažu ögkü-jü či keġebe.
sentences.l: Own-elder-sister, if-came, hiding, give? you said.
sentences.i: If your sister came, would you hide and give (her up)?" he said.
sentences.n: Egeči-jen is 'one's own elder sister' with the reflexive -jen. ireġesü is 'if (she) came'. žailažu is 'hiding, avoiding' (Ming 躱着). ögkü-jü is ög- 'to give' with the future -kü and an interrogative -jü (Ming 與麽, 'give?'). The meaning of this line is uncertain; I take 'give' to mean 'give up, yield', as an offer from Yesügen to give way to her sister, and the 'hiding' to be the same offer. keġebe is 'he said'.

morph.gloss: to hide, to avoid (Ming 躱) [躱着]

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun ügülerün:
sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun speaking-when:
sentences.i: Yesügen Qatun said:
sentences.n: Frame, as before.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.t: Qaγan sojur- γaγ̇asu egeči-jen ele üžeġesü egeči-deġen žailasu" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Qaγan, if-bestowing, own-elder-sister, indeed, if-I-see, to-own-elder-sister I-hide" said.
sentences.i: "If the Qahan shows favour, then if I see my sister, I shall step aside for her," she said.
sentences.n: sojur-γaγ̇asu is the same word as above, split by the print. ele is the emphatic 'but, only' (Ming 但). üžeġesü is üže- 'to see' with the conditional (Ming 見呵). žailasu is žaila- 'to hide, to avoid' with a first-person ending (Ming 躱我 'I hide'); I render it as 'step aside' on the strength of the sense in context, not of the Ming, and mark the reading as probable and not sure. egeči-deġen is 'to one's own sister' with the reflexive -deġen (Ming 姐姐 自的行).

morph.gloss: to bestow, to show favour [恩賜]
conditional: 'if, when' (Ming 呵; printed apart from sojur-) [呵]
emphatic particle: only, but (Ming 但) [但]
reflexive-possessive with dative: 'to one's own' (Ming 自的行)
to hide, to avoid, to step aside (Ming 躱) [躱我]
first-person optative/conditional ending (reading uncertain; Ming 我 'I')

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ tuṅqaγ̇ažu eriġülüġsü
sentences.l: This word-in, Chinggis Qaγan decree proclaiming, if-having-sought,
sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan issued a decree and had her sought,
sentences.n: tuṅqaγ̇ažu 'proclaiming' (Ming 傅着) is from tuṅqaγ 'a notice, a proclamation'. eriġülüġsü is the causative of eri- 'to seek' with a conditional (Ming 敎尋呵). The sentence is long and I have cut it at this point; the next unit says whom they found.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to proclaim, to send word (Ming 傅着) [傅着]

sentences.t: ögdegsen küregen-lüġe qamtu hoilažu jabuqu-ji bidan-u čeriġüd žolγažuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Given son-in-law with, together forest-in going-ACC, our soldiers met-had.
sentences.i: and our soldiers came upon her going together through the forest with the man to whom she had been given.
sentences.n: ögdegsen küregen-lüġe is 'together with the son-in-law who had been given' (Ming 與了的 女壻 一同); lüġe is the comitative. hoilažu is hoi 'forest' made into a verb (Ming 林裏). jabuqu-ji is the participle 'going' in the accusative (Ming 行的行): the object of žolγažuγ̇ui 'met, came upon' (Ming 遇着有來). I take the missing object ('her') from the sense. bidan-u čeriġüd 'our soldiers' is the subject.

morph.gloss: verbal: to go into the forest (Ming 林裏)
to go, to travel [行的 行]
to meet, to come upon [遇着有來]

sentences.t: Ere in-ü dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Husband, his, fled.
sentences.i: Her husband got away.
sentences.n: ere is 'husband' or 'man' (Ming 丈夫); in-ü is 'his'. dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u is the past of a verb whose root I take to be duta- 'to lack, to slip away' (Ming 走了有來 'ran off'), a first reading.

morph.gloss: to be missing, to slip away (Ming 走了) [走了有來]

sentences.t: Jesüi Qatun-i tende abčiraba.
sentences.l: Jesüi Qatun-ACC there brought.
sentences.i: They brought Yesui Qatun there.
sentences.n: abčiraba is ab- 'to take' joined with ire- 'to come': 'take and come', the usual 'to bring' (Ming 將來了). tende is 'there, to him'.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun Egeči-jen üže- ġed
sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun, own-elder-sister, having-seen,
sentences.i: Yesügen Qatun, seeing her sister,
sentences.n: üže- 'to see' is printed apart from its converb -ġed, which I join as 'having seen' (Ming 見了). The first clause of a long sentence continues in the next unit.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.t: urida ügülegsen üge-dür kürün bosču saγ̇uγsan saγ̇urin- dür(i)-jen saγ̇ulžu mün öġesün doro saγ̇ubi.
sentences.l: Before spoken word-in arriving, rising, sat-where own-seat-in seating, same own below sat.
sentences.i: as she had said before, rose and seated her sister in the place where she herself had sat, and sat down below her.
sentences.n: I read urida ügülegsen üge-dür kürün as 'in accordance with the word she had said before' (Ming 先前說了的言語裏到着, 'arriving at the word said earlier'); kür- 'to reach' with a converb. bosču is bos- 'to rise'. saγ̇uγsan saγ̇urin-dür-i-jen is 'in her own seat where she had sat': saγ̇urin 'seat' (Ming 位子) is printed with a hyphen and the ending on the next word. saγ̇ulžu is the causative, 'making sit'. mün öġesün doro saγ̇ubi: 'that very own self, below, sat' (Ming 他自己下坐了). The one unit is long; it is a single sentence in the Mongol and the converb chain is not cut here.

morph.gloss: seat, place to sit (Ming 位子; printed with a hyphen, the ending -dür follows on the next word) [位子]
the same, that very, also (Ming 他) [他]

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun-u üge-dür adali boldažu Čiṅgis Qaγan oin-dur(i)-jan oroγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun's word-in like being-made, Chinggis Qaγan, mind-in-own, making-enter,
sentences.i: Taking Yesügen Qatun's words to heart, Chinggis Qahan
sentences.n: adali boldažu is 'being made like' (Ming 相似被做着, 'being similar'); boldažu is bol- with the passive -da-. I take it as 'being matched with her word', and the English 'taking to heart' follows oroγ̇ulžu 'making enter' (the causative of oro- 'to enter') after oin-dur(i)-jan 'in his own mind' (Ming 情懷 自的行). That is, he let her words enter his thoughts. The Ming gives the parts, not the idiom, and the rendering is a reading. The unit ends where the subject continues in the next.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
mind, feeling, wits (Ming 情懷) [情懷 自的行]

sentences.t: Jesüi Qatun-i abču žerge-dür saγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Jesüi Qatun-ACC taking, rank-in seated.
sentences.i: took Yesui Qatun and seated her in the ranks of his wives.
sentences.n: žerge is 'rank, row' (Ming 列位) and the dative-locative gives 'in the row'. The Mongol does not say 'of wives', but the sense of the preceding story requires it, and Yesui is called Qatun. abču is ab- 'to take' with -ču (Ming 要着). saγ̇ulba is the causative 'made sit' with the past -ba.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]
rank, row, place in a line (Ming 列位) [列位 裏]

sentences.t: Tatar irgen-i daγ̇ulin baražu nigen üdür Čiṅgis Qaγan γada saγ̇užu undalaldurun
sentences.l: Tatar people-ACC plundering, finishing, one day, Chinggis Qaγan outside sitting, drinking-together-when,
sentences.i: After he had finished plundering the Tatar people, one day Chinggis Qahan was sitting outside, drinking with others,
sentences.n: daγ̇ulin baražu is the same pair as in line 2 (Ming 擄了着 'plundered, finished'). irgen-i takes the accusative, Ming 行. nigen üdür is 'one day'. undalaldurun is unda- 'to drink' with a verbal -la- and the reciprocal -ldu- (Ming 共飮時), 'when drinking together'. The sentence continues in the next unit with the circumstance of the drinking.

morph.gloss: to be finished, to finish [了着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Jesüi Qatun Jesügen Qatun žirin-ü dunda saγ̇užu undalaldun büküi-dür Jesüi Qatun jekede seġürelbi.
sentences.l: Jesüi Qatun, Jesügen Qatun, two's between sitting, drinking-together being-when, Jesüi Qatun greatly sighed.
sentences.i: and while Yesui Qatun and Yesügen Qatun sat on either side of him, Yesui Qatun sighed deeply.
sentences.n: žirin-ü dunda is 'between the two' (Ming 兩箇的中間). undalaldun is the converb 'drinking together'; büküi-dür is the participle büküi with -dür, 'at the being, while' (Ming 有時). jekede is the dative-locative of jeke 'great', used as an adverb 'greatly' (Ming 大行). seġürelbi is a verb from seġüre- 'to sigh' (Ming 嘆息了), and its -bi is the past. The text gives no reason for the sigh; I would not guess one.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan dotora-γ̇an sedkižü Boγ̇orču Muqali-tan nojad-i urižu ireġülžü ügülerün:
sentences.l: There Chinggis Qaγan, inside-own thinking, Bo'orchu, Muqali-and-others, noyans-ACC summoning, causing-to-come, speaking-when:
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan, turning it over in his mind, summoned Bo'orchu, Muqali and the other noyans, and said:
sentences.n: dotora-γ̇an is 'inside oneself' (Ming 內 自的行), a reflexive; sedkižü is sedki- 'to think'. Muqali-tan has -tan 'and the like' (Ming 等), and nojad-i is nojan 'noyan' (plural -d) in the accusative. urižu is uri- 'to call' and ireġülžü is ire- 'to come' made causative (Ming 敎來着), so 'calling, making come'; the two are a pair, translated as 'summoned'. The unit is a chain of five converbs and the verb is ügülerün 'speaking'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (Ming 內 自的行)
Bo'orchu, a man's name (Ming 人名) [(人)名]
Muqali, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名 等]
and the like, and others (Ming 等)
noyan, lord, commander (Ming 官人) [官人每(行)]

sentences.t: "Ta ede ele čiγ̇uluγsad haran büġüdeġer aimaγ aimaγ baidqun;
sentences.l: "You, these indeed assembled commoners, all, tribe by tribe, stand;
sentences.i: "All of you who are gathered here, stand, each in his own tribe;
sentences.n: Ta is 'you' (plural, Ming 您). ede ele čiγuluγsad haran is 'these, indeed, assembled commoners' (Ming 這的每 但 聚會的每 人). čiγuluγsad is the plural participle of čiγul- 'to assemble'. büġüdeġer 'all together' (Ming 都) is an adverb. aimaγ aimaγ is repeated (Ming 部落 部落) and means 'tribe by tribe'. baidqun is bai- 'to stand' with an imperative ending (Ming 立您 'stand, you'); the parts of the ending are uncertain, the sense is not.

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, only (Ming 但) [但]
to assemble, to gather [聚會的(每)]
plural past participle: 'those assembled' (Ming 聚會的每)
all together, all of them (Ming 都) [都︀]
to stand, to be placed [立您]

sentences.t: öġer-eče busu aimaγ-un küġün-i öġere böldeidgedkün" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: from-own, other tribe's person-ACC apart, make-solitary" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: and leave apart, by himself, any man of another tribe than his own." So he decreed.
sentences.n: öġer-eče busu is 'other than oneself' (Ming 自巳裏 別): öġer is 'own, self'. aimaγ-un küġün-i 'a man of a tribe' (genitive and accusative). öġere is 'apart' (Ming glosses it with a rare character that does not print here). böldeidgedkün is a verb whose root I take to be böldei- 'to be solitary' (Ming 敎孤零您 'make (him) lonely'), with a causative and an imperative; the form is uncertain and the sense comes mainly from the Ming. keġen žarliγ bolba closes the speech, 'saying, a decree was made'.

morph.gloss: other, one's own separate (Ming 自巳 'oneself') [自巳裏]
to be solitary, to be left alone (Ming 孤零) [敎孤零您]
causative imperative: 'make (him) be -' (Ming 敎 ... 您; form uncertain)

sentences.t: Tedüi aimaγ aimak(i)-jar(i)-jan baiγ̇asu nigen žalaγ̇ui sain gürümele küġün aimaγ̇ud-ača öġre baiba.
sentences.l: So-much tribe, tribe-own, stood-when, one young good slender man, from-the-tribes apart stood.
sentences.i: When the tribes had so stood, each by itself, one young, fine, slender man stood apart from the tribes.
sentences.n: baiγ̇asu is bai- 'to stand' with the conditional 'when' (Ming 立呵). žalaγ̇ui is 'young' (Ming 年少) and gürümele is 'slender' (Ming 苗條); the Ming picks out his build. aimaγ̇ud-ača is the plural with the ablative, 'from the tribes' (Ming 部落每的 行). The unit has a double reduplication, aimaγ and aimak(i)-jar(i)-jan, which I read as 'tribe by tribe, each in its own'; the -jar is the same doubtful instrumental as before.

morph.gloss: to stand, to be placed [立呵]
to stand, to be placed [立了]

sentences.t: "Či jaγ̇un küġün bi" kēġesü
sentences.l: "You what person are?" when-said,
sentences.i: "What man are you?" he was asked,
sentences.n: Či 'you', jaγ̇un 'what' (Ming 甚), küġün 'person'. bi 'is, exists' (Ming 有) closes the quotation. kēġesü is keġe- 'to say' with a conditional, 'if/when (one) said', written with a long vowel (Ming 說呵).

sentences.t: tere küġün ügülerün:
sentences.l: that person speaking-when:
sentences.i: and the man said:
sentences.n: Frame.

sentences.t: "Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü Jesüi neretei ökin ögdegsen küregen küġün büleġe bi.
sentences.l: "Tatar's Jeke-Čeren's Jesüi named daughter, given-of son-in-law, person was I.
sentences.i: "I was the son-in-law, given to the daughter of the Tatar Jeke-Cheren, named Yesui.
sentences.n: Here we learn who the stranger is: the husband of Yesui, who had slipped away in §155. Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü Jesüi neretei ökin is 'the daughter named Yesui of Jeke-Cheren of the Tatars' (nere 'name', -tei 'having'). ögdegsen küregen is 'the son-in-law who had been given' (Ming 被與的 女壻). küġün büleġe bi is 'I was a person'; büleġe is 'was' and bi 'I'. I read this as 'the man who had been given the daughter as wife', i.e. her husband; the Mongol uses küregen for the man who has married into a household.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Cheren, a man's name [人名 的]

sentences.t: Daisun-a daγ̇uliγdarun ajužu buruγ̇udču jabužu edöġe amaurliba že
sentences.l: Enemy-by being-plundered-when, fearing, fleeing, going, now peace-found indeed"
sentences.i: When the enemy overran us I was afraid and fled and went about; now I have found peace,"
sentences.n: daisun-a daγ̇uliγdarun is 'when plundered by the enemy' (daγ̇uli- with the passive -γda- and -run; the dative -a marks the agent, Ming 敵行 被據時). ajužu is aju- 'to fear' (Ming 怕著). buruγ̇udču is a verb of fleeing, buruγ̇u- with -d- and -ču (Ming 躱着). amaurliba is 'found ease' (Ming 安妥了). že is the closing particle. The speech goes on in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to plunder, to carry off [被據時]
verbal: to hide, to flee (Ming 躱)
to be at ease, to find peace (Ming 安妥) [安妥了]
emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.t: keġen irežü olon haran dotora jaγ̇u tamiγ- daqu keġežü jabulaγ̇a" keġebe
sentences.l: saying, coming, many commoners among, whom recognise saying, went-about" said.
sentences.i: I came and went about among the many people, not knowing whom to acknowledge," he said.
sentences.n: The words jaγ̇u tamiγ-daqu keġežü are the obscure ones: jaγ̇u 'what, how' (Ming 怎), tamiγ-daqu 'to know, to recognise' (Ming 認的), keġežü 'saying'. I read 'saying to himself, how shall I recognise (anyone)', i.e. he was a stranger looking for someone to attach himself to; the Ming does not show whether he was looking for his own people or for new ones. jabulaγ̇a is jabu- 'to go' with a verbal -la- and -γ̇a (Ming 行來 'went about').

morph.gloss: recognition; with -da- 'to know, to recognise' (Ming 認) [認]

sentences.t: Ene üge-ji Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a öčiġešü žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: This word-ACC Chinggis Qaγan-to reporting, decree being-when:
sentences.i: When this was reported to Chinggis Qahan, he decreed:
sentences.n: ene üge-ji is 'this word' with the accusative; Qaγ̇an-a is 'to the Qahan' (Ming 皇帝 行). öčiġešü is a verb of reporting up (Ming 奏呵, 'if/when reported'); the root is not clear to me. žarliγ bolurun is the decree formula, as in line 117.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to say, to report to a superior (Ming 奏) [奏呵]

sentences.t: "Mün kü daisu sedkižü oγ̇orčaγ bolžu jabužuγ̇u.
sentences.l: "Indeed also rebel thinking, robber being, going-had.
sentences.i: "He had meant to rebel; he was going about as a robber.
sentences.n: mün kü is 'indeed, just so' (Ming 只也). daisu is 'to be hostile, to rebel' (Ming 反), a reading, and I take sedkižü to mean 'planning'. oγ̇orčaγ is 'robber' (Ming 劫賊). jabužuγ̇u is the past 'had gone, had been going' (Ming 行有來). The Mongol does not say 'he', but a decree about the man is plain.

morph.gloss: just, indeed (emphatic particle; Ming 也) [也]
to be hostile, to rebel (Ming 反; reading uncertain) [反]

sentences.t: Edöġe jaγ̇u kürüre irežüġü.
sentences.l: Now what spying, come.
sentences.i: Now what has he come to spy out?
sentences.n: kürüre is read as 'to spy, to watch for a chance' (Ming 窺伺); I have no form for it. irežüġü is 'has come' (Ming 來有).

morph.gloss: to spy, to watch for a chance (Ming 窺伺; reading uncertain) [窺伺]

sentences.t: In-ü metüs-i čiγ̇un-dur uliba. Jaγ̇u saγ̇aramui;
sentences.l: His likes-ACC linchpin-at compared. What doubting?
sentences.i: Such men as he have been measured against the linchpin. Why doubt?
sentences.n: in-ü metüs-i is 'those like him' (metü 'like', plural -s, accusative; Ming 似他般的每行). čiγ̇un-dur uliba is the formula of lines 28–38: 'compared at the linchpin' (Ming 比了). I take it here as 'dealt with by the rule of the linchpin', that is, killed. saγ̇aramui is saγ̇ara- 'to doubt' with the present -mui (Ming 疑).

morph.gloss: like, such as [似他般的每(行)]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to doubt, to suspect (Ming 疑) [疑]

sentences.t: nidün-ü ečine gedkün" keġebe.
sentences.l: Eyes' behind cast-away" said.
sentences.i: Put him out of our sight," he said.
sentences.n: nidün-ü ečine is 'behind the eyes' (Ming 眼的背處行): 'out of sight'. gedkün is read as a verb 'to cast aside' (Ming 棄了您) with an imperative; the root is uncertain. The order is carried out in the next unit, which shows the sense is 'put to death'.

morph.gloss: behind, at the back (Ming 背處) [背處行]
to cast aside, to throw away (Ming 棄了; reading uncertain) [棄了您]

sentences.t: Tedüi-kü mököriġülbe.
sentences.l: Thereupon had-cut-down.
sentences.i: At once they had him beheaded.
sentences.n: tedüi-kü is 'thereupon, at once' (Ming 隨卽). mököriġülbe is a causative of a verb 'to cut, to behead' (Ming 斬了, 'cut down'): 'made (someone) cut off (his head)'. This ends §156.

morph.gloss: to cut, to behead (Ming 斬) [斬了]

sentences.t: Mün noγai žil Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)i Tatar irgen-dür morilaγsan-dur
sentences.l: Same dog year, Chinggis Qaγan, Tatar people-to, horse-mounting-when,
sentences.i: In the same Dog year, when Chinggis Qahan took the field against the Tatar people,
sentences.n: A § that begins, as the Ming does, with the year (mün noγai žil 'the same dog year'). I take Qaγan-(n)i as having the accusative or a reflexive ending (Ming 行), but the case is unclear to me. morilaγsan-dur is mori 'horse' with -la- 'to use' and the participle -γsan with -dur 'at, when' (Ming 上馬了 時), 'when (one) had mounted', that is, taken the field.

morph.gloss: the same, that very (Ming 只) [只]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
verbal: to ride, to take the field
dative-locative: at, when (Ming 上馬了時)

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān Merkid irgen-dür morilažu Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ji Barγužin-Tögüm žüg hüldežü
sentences.l: Wang Qan, Merkid people-to, horse-mounting, Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ACC Barγužin-Tögüm toward chasing,
sentences.i: the Wang Qan rode against the Merkid people and chased Toqto'a Beki toward Barguzin-Tögüm,
sentences.n: Waṅ-Qān is the Kereid ruler; the Ming has 人名. Merkid is a people (Ming 種(名)的). Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ji takes the accusative (Ming 人名行); Barγužin-Tögüm is a place (Ming 地名) and žüg is 'toward, in the direction' (Ming 往). hüldežü is hülde- 'to chase' (Ming 追着). The chain goes on for three more units; I cut it where the objects change.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, the Kereid ruler (Ming 人名) [人名]
verbal: to ride, to take the field
Toqto'a Beki, a Merkid chief (Ming 人名) [人名 行]
Barguzin-Tögüm, a place (Ming 地名) [地名]

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-jin jeke köġün Tögüs- Beki-ji alažu
sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a's great son Tögüs-Beki-ACC killing,
sentences.i: killed Toqto'a's eldest son, Tögüs-Beki,
sentences.n: Toγtoγ̇a-jin is the genitive after a vowel. jeke köġün is 'great son' (Ming 大 子), which I take as 'eldest'. The name is printed Tögüs- / Beki-ji, split by the line (Ming 人 名行); Tögüs-Beki is one man, and Beki is a title. alažu is ala- 'to kill'.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
Tögüs, a name (the Ming reads it with the next word) [人]

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-jin Quntuγtai, Čaγ̇arun žirin ökid in-ü qatud in-ü abču
sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a's Quntuγtai, Čaγ̇arun two daughters, his wives, his taking,
sentences.i: took Toqto'a's two daughters, Quntuqtai and Cha'arun, as his wives,
sentences.n: žirin ökid is 'two daughters' (ökid is the plural of ökin; Ming 兩箇 女每); the two names are printed with Ming 女名. in-ü qatud in-ü abču is the puzzle: 'his wives, his, taking'. in-ü is 'his', and the Ming has 他的 for both. Either 'taking them for his wives' (the first in-ü pointing to the Wang Qan) or 'taking Toqto'a's daughters, his wives', and I take the first. Which 'his' goes with which is left open; the next unit uses in-ü again for Toqto'a's people.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
Quntuqtai, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]
Chaqarun, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]

sentences.t: Qutu, Čilaγ̇un qojar köġüd-i in-ü irge selte daγ̇uližu
sentences.l: Qutu, Čilaγ̇un two sons-ACC, his people together-with plundering,
sentences.i: and carried off the two sons, Qutu and Chila'un, together with their people,
sentences.n: Qutu and Čilaγ̇un are 'son names' (Ming 子名); qojar köġüd-i is 'the two sons' (plural köġüd, accusative; Ming 兩箇 兒子每行). in-ü irge selte is 'with his people' (Ming 他的 百姓 連): irge is a short form of irgen. daγ̇uližu is the converb 'plundering' (Ming 擄着), so the three units 'chasing, killing, taking, plundering' all belong to one chain that I cut up.

morph.gloss: Qutu, a son's name (Ming 子名) [子名]
Chilaun, a son's name (Ming 子名) [子名]
people (variant of irgen; Ming 百姓) [百姓]
to plunder, to carry off [擄着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a jaγ̇u ber ese ögbe.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-to what even not gave.
sentences.i: and gave Chinggis Qahan nothing at all.
sentences.n: A short coda, and the one clause with a main verb that is not a converb. Qaγ̇an-a is 'to the Qahan' (Ming 皇帝 行). jaγ̇u ber 'what even' (Ming 甚麽 也), with ese 'not' (Ming 不曾), gives 'not anything at all'; ese is the negative of a past action, 'did not give' (Ming 與了, ögbe). The subject is the Wang Qan, who did not share with Chinggis; the Mongol does not state the subject, and this is the Ming's reading too.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
not (negates a past action; Ming 不曾) [不曾]
